sections.title: 31-34 ALLAH'S COMMANDMENT TO THE WIVES OF PROPHET MUHAMMAD

translation.text: But whoever of you is obedient to Allah and His Messenger and does good deeds, Allah will double her reward. We have prepared for her a generous provision.

commentary.text: DEFINITION OF SUCCESS
Iman + good deeds = Success (Paradise)

The reason for giving a double punishment for a sin and a double reward for a good work is that those whom Allah SWT honors with a high rank in society generally become the leaders of men and the majority of the people follow them for good or for evil. Thus, their evil does not remain their own evil (hidden) but becomes the cause of a people’s degeneration, and their goodness does not remain their own goodness but becomes the cause of true success for many others. Therefore, when they commit evil, they are punished for their own as well as for others degeneration, and when they do good they are not only rewarded for their own good works but also for those they guided.
Context: The wives of the Prophet (PBUH) are role models and teachers for the Muslim ummah and their sacrifice was greater.

translation.text: Wives of the Prophet, you are not like other women. If you fear Allah, do not be too complaisant in your speech lest those with diseased hearts should covet you; but speak in a straight forward manner.

commentary.text: These Ayat’s are regarding the commandments of pardah -- introduced in Islam. Only the wives of the Prophet (PBUH) have been addressed because when a pure way of life begins from the Prophet’s (PBUH) house, it will be followed by other Muslim households as the Prophet's (PBUH) house was looked upon as a model to follow.

Some people, when they see that these Ayat’s have been addressed only to the wives of the Prophet (PBUH), assert that these commandments were only meant for them. However, could Allah SWT have intended that only the wives of the Prophet (PBUH) should obey Allah SWT and His Prophet (PBUH).

As for the sentence, “You are not like any other women,” it also does not mean that other Muslim women should come out in full makeup and should talk to men coquettishly and flirt with them. This style of narration is just as if a man would tell his child, “You are not like the common children of the street: you should not use abusive language.” From this no sensible person would ever conclude that the speaker regarded only his own child using abusive language as bad; as for others he would not mind if they used abusive language.

Speech: There is no harm if a man is spoken to in case of a genuine need, but on such an occasion the woman’s tone and manner of speech should be such as does not let the man think that he could cherish any false hope from her. There should be no undue softness in her tone, no allurement in her conversation, no consciously affected mellowness in her voice, which should excite the male hearer’s emotions and encourage him to make advances.
If this Ayat is read together with Surah An-Nur, Ayat 31, in which Allah SWT says:

translation.text: And tell the believing women to lower their gaze and guard their chastity, and not to reveal their adornments except what normally appears. Let them draw their veils over their chests, and not reveal their ˹hidden˺ adornments except to their husbands, their fathers, their fathers-in-law, their sons, their stepsons, their brothers, their brothers’ sons or sisters’ sons, their fellow women, those ˹bondwomen˺ in their possession, male attendants with no desire, or children who are still unaware of women’s nakedness. Let them not stomp their feet, drawing attention to their hidden adornments. Turn to Allah in repentance all together, O believers, so that you may be successful.

commentary.text: The intention of our Lord clearly seems to be that the women should not attract other men by their voice or the jingle of their ornaments unnecessarily, and if at all they have to speak to men, they should speak to them in an unaffected tone and manner.

That is why it is forbidden for the woman to pronounce the call to the Prayer (Azan). Moreover, if a woman is attending a congregational prayer and the Imam commits a mistake, she is not permitted to say," Subhan-Allah" like the males but should only tap her hands to call the imam's attention to the error.
Note: Important to note that it is not forbidden for women to talk to men.
FYI -- Most customer service are women because the voice of the women is universally deemed attractive.

arabic_lines: وَقَرۡنَ فِىۡ بُيُوۡتِكُنَّ وَلَا تَبَـرَّجۡنَ تَبَرُّجَ الۡجَاهِلِيَّةِ الۡاُوۡلٰى وَاَقِمۡنَ الصَّلٰوةَ وَاٰتِيۡنَ الزَّكٰوةَ وَاَطِعۡنَ اللّٰهَ وَرَسُوۡلَهٗ ؕ اِنَّمَا يُرِيۡدُ اللّٰهُ لِيُذۡهِبَ عَنۡكُمُ الرِّجۡسَ اَهۡلَ الۡبَيۡتِ وَيُطَهِّرَكُمۡ تَطۡهِيۡرًا ۚ

translation.text:
And stay وَقَرۡنَ (qarna) in your homes and do not go about displaying تَبَـرَّجۡنَ تَبَرُّجَ (tabarruj)
your allurements as in the former Time of Ignorance الۡجَاهِلِيَّةِ(jahiliyyat al-ula). Establish Prayer, give Zakat, and obey Allah and His Messenger. Allah only wishes to remove uncleanness from you, O members of the (Prophet's) household  اَهۡلَ الۡبَيۡتِ ( ahl al-bait), and to purify you completely.

commentary.text: The word qarna وَقَرۡنَ is derived from qarar which means: remaining in a particular state, permanence and in the second sense: “live peacefully, sit with dignity.” In both cases the Ayat means that the woman’s real sphere of activity is her home; she should carry out her functions within that sphere peacefully, and she should come out of the house only in case of a genuine need.

This meaning is clear from the words of the Ayat itself and a hadith reinforces this concept. Hafiz Abu Bakr Bazzar related that the women made a submission to the Prophet (PBUH), saying: “All kinds of virtues have been secured by the men: they fight and accomplish great deeds in the way of Allah SWT. What should we do that we may also get a reward equal to that of the warriors?” The Prophet (PBUH) replied: “The one who sits in her house from among you; will attain the reward of the warriors.” What he meant was: The warrior can fight confidently and with full peace of the mind in the way of Allah SWT only when he is sure that all is well at home. His wife is there to look after the house and the children, and there is no cause for him to worry that she will betray him in his absence. The woman who will provide him this satisfaction and peace of the mind will be an equal partner with him in his fighting though she will be sitting back at home.
In this Ayat two important words have been used, which must be understood for the proper understanding of its intention. They are "tabarruj" and "jahiliyyat al-ula."

The word "tabarruj," تَبَـرَّجۡنَ in Arabic means to become manifest and appear openly before others. The Arabs use the word baraj for every conspicuous and elevated object. A burj (tower) is so called because of its prominence and elevation i.e. Burj Khalifa. A sailboat is called barijah, because its sails become visible from a distance. The word "tabarruj," when used in respect of a woman means not doing anything that attracts the attention of men, for example, walk in an alluring manner, display of her beautifications,  hair and chest etc. In essence, that a woman should make herself conspicuous by displaying herself to attract the attention of men.

"Jahiliyyat," الۡجَاهِلِيَّةِ in the Islamic terminology is every such conduct that goes against Islamic culture, civilization, morality and Islamic way of thinking and behavior. Thus, jahiliyyat al-ula means all those evils in which the Arabs of the pre-Islamic days and the people of the entire world were involved.

This explanation makes it abundantly clear that what Allah SWT forbids is that women step out of their houses showing off their physical charms and beauty. He instructs them to stay in their houses because their real sphere of activity is their home and not the world outside. However, if they have to move out of their house for an outdoor duty, they should not move out as the women used to do in the pre-Islamic days of ignorance. It does not behoove a Muslim woman to walk out fully made up in tightfitting or transparent dresses. These are the ways of ignorance that Islam does not approve.

The word "ahl al-bait," اَهۡلَ الۡبَيۡتِ (people of the house/household) here implies the wives of the Prophet (PBUH), because the address begins with: “O wives of the Prophet,” Just like the Prophet (PBUH), is a role model for being the best, father, husband, leader, master, etc. similarly the wives of the Prophet (PBUH) are role models for all Believing woman.
Salat and zakat are mentioned after displaying of beauty. These two commandments are also to purify you.

FYI – 100 years ago every dignified, high-class woman in the West/USA would cover her hair/head with a hat or headscarf. Only peasants went without head cover. Even today at the races of Ascot woman wear hats.

translation.text: ˹Always˺ remember what is recited in your homes of Allah’s revelations and ˹prophetic˺ wisdom. Surely Allah is Most Subtle, All-Aware.

commentary.text: Allah SWT tells the wives of the Prophet and then by default all Muslim women to recite and convey the Quran. Take the Quran seriously and make time to study the Quran within your homes. Emphasis is on using time productively.

Lesson: A woman is the best teacher for her children and grandchildren etc. After marriage or rather especially after marriage a woman must study her deen so that she can inspire and guide the next generation.

sections.title: 35-36 IT IS NOT FITTING FOR BELIEVERS TO HAVE OPTION IN WHAT HAS BEEN DECIDED BY ALLAH AND HIS RASOOL

translation.text: Surely the men who submit (to Allah) and the women who submit (to Allah), the men who have faith and the women who have faith, the men who are obedient and the women who are obedient the men who are truthful and the women who are truthful; the men who are steadfast and the women who are steadfast, the men who humble themselves (to Allah) and the women who humble themselves (to Allah), the men who give alms and the women who give alms, the men who fast and the women who fast, the men who guard their chastity and the women who guard their chastity, the men who remember Allah much and the women who remember Allah much: for them has Allah prepared forgiveness and a mighty reward.

commentary.text: SUMMARY OF CHARACTERISTICS OF AN IDEA MUSLIM (MAN AND WOMAN)

These characteristics include both outward submission and spiritual submission that will lead to success. (i) Submission (ii) Faith/Belief (iii) Obedience/Devout (iv) Truthful (v) Steadfastness/Patience (vi) Humility (vii) Charity (viii) Chastity (ix) Fasting (x) Remember Allah SWT Much.
Note: Ayat 35 in surah Nur mentions the Nur/light of a Believer that is on the inside/hidden. Here Ayat 35 discusses what a Believer should look like on the outside/apparent.
Lesson: Reflect upon and develop these traits within yourself.

translation.text: It does not behove a believer, male or female, that when Allah and His Messenger have decided an affair they should exercise their choice. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has strayed to manifest error.

commentary.text: To be a Muslim means to surrender one’s freedom of opinion and action before Allah SWT and His Messenger. This is a very important and at times very difficult concept but must retain top priority in our lives.
Lesson: When a command comes from Allah SWT then we do not have the option to exercise our personal choice. Our desire is not the leader rather Allah SWT is the Leader and our Raab.
From here begin the Ayats that were revealed in connection with the Prophet’s (PBUH) marriage with Zainab (may Allah be pleased with her).

sections.title: 37-40 ALLAH COMMANDED PROPHET MUHAMMAD TO MARRY THE DIVORCED WIFE OF HIS ADOPTED SON ZAID AND MUHAMMAD IS NOT THE FATHER OF ANY OF YOUR MEN BUT A RASOOL AND SEAL OF THE PROPHETHOOD

translation.text: And ˹remember, O Prophet,˺ when you said to the one for whom Allah has done a favour and you ˹too˺ have done a favour, “Keep your wife and fear Allah,” while concealing within yourself what Allah was going to reveal. And ˹so˺ you were considering the people, whereas Allah was more worthy of your consideration. So when Zaid totally lost interest in ˹keeping˺ his wife, We gave her to you in marriage, so that there would be no blame on the believers for marrying the ex-wives of their adopted sons after their divorce. And Allah’s command is totally binding.

commentary.text: The Prophet married his adopted son (and freed slave) Zaid to his first cousin Zainab. However, they could not make the marriage work. When Zaid asked permission to divorce Zainab the Prophet diswaded him saying, “Keep your wife and fear Allah.” This was because the Prophet (PBUH) knew that Allah SWT had intended for him a marriage to Zainab and feared what people would say.

The wrong customs regarding adopted relations had become so entrenched and prevalent in Arabia, that Allah’s Messenger himself had to take the initiative to abolish them. Therefore, Allah SWT arranged this marriage not for the sake of adding a wife to the Prophet’s (PBUH) household but for enforcing an important social change.

This nikkah was performed by Allah SWT Himself. Allah SWT says, "We gave her to you in marriage…," thus Allah SWT was her wali (guardian) in this marriage in the sense that He revealed to the Prophet that he should go in unto her without any Wali, contractual agreement, dowry or witnesses among mankind.
And thus this cultural pagan superstition and taboo about adopted sons being like real sons was destroyed.

Lesson: As Muslims when Allah SWT orders us to do something we should not feel the slightest hesitation/burden or discomfort executing the command. Also note that we cannot water down change, or feel the need to justify Allah SWT laws such as hijab, multiple marriages etc.

arabic_lines: مَا كَانَ مُحَمَّدٌ اَبَآ اَحَدٍ مِّنۡ رِّجَالِكُمۡ وَلٰـكِنۡ رَّسُوۡلَ اللّٰهِ وَخَاتَمَ النَّبِيّٖنَ ؕ وَكَانَ اللّٰهُ بِكُلِّ شَىۡءٍ عَلِيۡمًا

translation.text: Muhammad is not the father of any of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the seal of the Prophets. Allah has full knowledge of everything.

commentary.text: This one sentence was at the root of all objections the opponents were raising in connection with this marriage of the Prophet (PBUH).

Their first objection was that he had married his own daughter-in-law, whereas according to his own law the son’s wife are forbidden for the father. This was answered by saying: “Muhammad is not the father of any of your men.” Zaid was not his real son, and so it was not unlawful to marry his divorced wife. Note: All of the Prophet’s (PBUH) sons died either in infancy or childhood infact Zaid too died during the life of the Prophet (PBUH).

Their second objection was that even if his adopted son was not his real son, was not necessary that he should have married his divorced wife? This was answered by saying: “But he is the Messenger of Allah.” That is, it was his duty as the Messenger of Allah to put an end to all kinds of prejudices about a lawful thing which custom and tradition had made unlawful without good reason and declare it to be lawful once again.

The point was stressed by saying: “and (he is) the seal of the Prophets.” سُوۡلَ اللّٰهِ وَخَاتَمَ النَّبِيّٖنَ The last of the Prophets. Now no other Prophet would be raised after him, therefore, it had become all the more necessary that he should himself root out the custom of ignorance.

To further emphasize this point, it was said: “Allah SWT has knowledge of everything.” that is, Allah SWT knows best why it was imperative to get the custom of ignorance rooted out at that juncture through the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) rather than let it remain as it was.

sections.title: 41-48 PROPHET IS SENT AS A BEARER OF GOOD NEWS, A WARNER AND A LAMP SPREADING LIGHT

translation.text: Believers, remember Allah much
and glorify Him morning and evening.

commentary.text: The Virtue of remembering Allah much

Remember and glorify Allah SWT much and all the time. Learn duas for entering the house, leaving the house, entering a market etc. Thus, no matter what you are doing keep your tongue moist with Allah SWT's remembrance. Glorify Allah SWT in the AM and PM via zikr-e- khaas and tasbeeh specific for this time.  Zikr of Allah SWT is like a shield against satan.
When you remember Allah SWT then He will remember you by sending His Mercy and Blessings upon you and so will His angels.
Hadith:
"Two Bedouins came to the Messenger of Allah and one of them said: `O Messenger of Allah, which of the people is best' He said: "The one whose life is long and whose deeds are good."

The other one said: `O Messenger of Allah, the laws of Islam are too much for us. Teach me something that I can adhere to.' He said,"Keep your tongue moist with the remembrance of Allah, may He be exalted".

arabic_lines: يٰۤـاَيُّهَا النَّبِىُّ اِنَّاۤ اَرۡسَلۡنٰكَ شَاهِدًا وَّمُبَشِّرًا وَّنَذِيۡرًا ۙ

translation.text: O Prophet, We have sent you forth as a witness, a bearer of good tidings, and a warner

commentary.text: The Attributes of the Messenger of Allah

A witness to Allah's Oneness, for there is no God except He, and a witness against mankind for their deeds on the Day of Resurrection. A bearer of glad tidings for the believers of a great reward, and a warner to the disbelievers of a great punishment.

arabic_lines: وَّدَاعِيًا اِلَى اللّٰهِ بِاِذۡنِهٖ وَسِرَاجًا مُّنِيۡرًا

translation.text: as one who calls people to Allah by His leave, and as a bright, shining lamp.

commentary.text: The mission of the Prophet (PBUH) is being described here which was to invite people to Allah SWT.  The parable or example of a lamp is being given that emits Nur or light so that we can see clearly. So the Prophet (PBUH) is our guide towards the truth.
Important to note that for anyone to convey the message of Allah SWT we must ask Allah SWT’s permission, His guidance and His assistance.

Attributes of the Prophet (PBUH): Warner وَّنَذِيۡرً (Nazir), Bearer of good news مُبَشِّرًا (Mubashir or Bushra), Witness شَاهِدً (Shahid), Bright, Shinning Lamp/lLight, وَسِرَاجًا مُّنِيۡرًا (Siraj/Momin).

translation.text: Give good news to the believers that they will have a great bounty from Allah.

commentary.text: DEFINITION OF SUCCESS
Iman = Huge bounty or bonus. (Beyond our imagination.)

arabic_lines: وَلَا تُطِعِ الۡكٰفِرِيۡنَ وَالۡمُنٰفِقِيۡنَ وَدَعۡ اَذٰٮهُمۡ وَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى اللّٰهِ ؕ وَكَفٰى بِاللّٰهِ وَكِيۡلًا

translation.text: Do not yield to the unbelievers and the hypocrites, and disregard the hurt that comes from them, and put your trust in Allah. Allah suffices as the Guardian to entrust one's affairs to.

commentary.text: Also see (33:3)
Again, it is mentioned that Allah SWT is sufficient as your provider, helper and guardian – so trust and rely upon Him alone.

sections.title: 49-52 DIVORCE WHEN NO IDDAT (WAITING PERIOD FOR REMARRIAGE) IS REQUIRED AND SPECIAL PERMISSION FOR PROPHET MUHAMMAD TO MARRY MORE THAN FOUR WIVES AND RESTRICTION ON PROPHET TO MARRY OR EXCHANGE THE PRESENT WIVES AFTER THIS COMMANDMENT

translation.text: Believers, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, you may not require them to observe a waiting period that you might reckon against them. So make provision for them and release them in an honourable manner.

commentary.text: The theme of marriage continues. This is a command upon which all scholars are in agreement, that if a woman is divorced before the marriage is consummated, she does not have to observe the `Iddah' (prescribed waiting period for divorce) and she may get married immediately to whomever she wishes. This is because there is no chance of her expecting a child. She should be given some monetary compensation and sent in an honorable manner (without creating difficulty).
The only exception, in this regard, is a woman whose husband died, in which case she has to observe an `Iddah’ of four months and ten days even if the marriage was not consummated.
Note: If the mehr has been fixed then ½ must be given (Surah Baqarah Ayat 241). However, if the mehr has not been fixed then give according to your capacity.

translation.text: O Prophet, We have made lawful for you your wives whose bridal dues you have paid, and the slave-girls you possess from among the prisoners of war, and the daughters of your paternal uncles and paternal aunts, and the daughters of your maternal uncles and maternal aunts who have migrated with you, and a believing woman who gives herself to the Prophet and whom he wants to take in marriage. (O Prophet), this privilege is yours alone to the exclusion of other believers. We know well what restrictions We have imposed upon them as regards their wives and those whom their right hands possess, (and have exempted you from those restrictions) that there may be no constraint upon you. Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.

commentary.text: The Women who are Lawful for the Prophet

This, in fact, is an answer to the objection of the people who said that Muhammad (PBUH) forbade others to keep more than four wives at a time but had himself taken a fifth wife. This objection was raised because at the time the Prophet (PBUH) married Zainab, he already had four wives.

Logic: The task entrusted to the Prophet (PBUH) was to convey the message of Islam via an all-inclusive education/training so as to mold a nation which was uncivilized not only from the Islamic point of view but from a general viewpoint as well, into a civilized and virtuous nation. For this purpose, it was not enough to train men but the training of women was equally necessary. However, the teachings/principles of social life and civilization forbade free mixing of the sexes, and thus it was not possible to impart direct training to the womenfolk. Therefore, to impart education/training to women, the Prophet (PBUH) married several women of different ages and mental capabilities. These women then imparted what was conveyed to them by the Prophet (PBUH) to the young, middle-aged and old women of the city and desert, teaching them the new principles of morality and civilization. A good example for such a teacher is Aisha who spent her whole life imparting the principles of Islam.

Moreover, the Prophet (PBUH) was also appointed to abolish the system of life of the pre-Islamic days of ignorance and replace it with the Islamic system of life practically. Under these conditions, besides other devices, it was also necessary that the Prophet (PBUH) marry in different families and clans in order to cement ties of friendship and put an end to enmities. Thus, the selection of the ladies whom he married was to some extent determined by this objective in addition to their personal qualities. By marring Aishah and Hafsah, he further strengthened and deepened the relations with Abu Bakr and Umar. Umm Salamah was the daughter of the family to which Abu Jahl and Khalid bin Walid belonged, and Umm Habibah was the daughter of Abu Sufyan. These marriages neutralized the enmity of these families to a large extent.
FYI – Tahajud was mandatory for the Prophet (PBUH) and he was not allowed to accept sadakah. These were some other exceptions exclusive to the Prophet (PBUH) only.

sections.title: 53-55 DO NOT ENTER THE HOUSES OF THE PROPHET WITHOUT PERMISSION, AND IF INVITED DO NOT SEEK LONG CONVERSATION AND DO NOT MARRY RASOOL'S WIVES AFTER HIS DEATH

translation.text: Believers, enter not the houses of the Prophet without his permission, nor wait for a meal to be prepared; instead enter when you are invited to eat, and when you have had the meal, disperse. Do not linger in idle talk. That is hurtful to the Prophet but he does not express it out of shyness; but Allah is not ashamed of speaking out the Truth. And if you were to ask the wives of the Prophet for something, ask from behind a curtain. (حِجَابٍ) (hijab) That is more apt for the cleanness of your hearts and theirs. It is not lawful for you to cause hurt to Allah's Messenger, nor to ever marry his wives after him. Surely that would be an enormous sin in Allah's sight.

commentary.text: The Etiquette of entering the Houses of the Prophet and the Command of Hijab

In ancient times the Arabs would enter one another’s houses unannounced thus deeming it unnecessary to knock or take permission for entry. This custom of ignorance gave rise to some serious evils. Therefore, in the beginning a rule was made in respect of the houses of the Prophet (PBUH) that no person, whether a close friend or a distant relative, could enter without permission. Then one year later in Surah An-Nur Ayat 27 (see below) a general command was given to enforce this rule when entering the homes of ALL Muslims.

translation.text: Believers! Enter not houses other than your own houses until you have obtained the permission of the inmates of those houses and have greeted them with peace. This is better for you. It is expected that you will observe this.

commentary.text: The second command in this connection. An uncivilized practice prevalent among the Arabs was that visitors would call on a friend or acquaintance right at the time of meals, or would come and prolong their stay until mealtime approached, thus often causing the master of the house great distress and embarrassment. He could neither be so discourteous as to tell the visitors to leave because it was his meal time, nor could he feed so many. Allah SWT disapproved of this practice and commanded that the visitors should go for meals to a house only when invited. This command did not in particular apply to the Prophet’s (PBUH) house only but the rule was initially enforced in that model household so that they become general rules of etiquette in the houses of the all-other Muslims as well.

Yet another reform needed was that after they had finished eating guests would sit down to endless gossip and discussions much to the inconvenience of the people of the house. The Prophet (PBUH) was also inconvenienced by this practice, but he would forbear and forget. However, on the day of the marriage feast of Zainab this practice crossed all limits. Thus, the command to disperse and not linger after the meal was revealed.

This Ayat is called “the Ayat of the veil.” Since the Prophet (PBUH) was visited by all kinds of the people, both good and bad hence the need for this command that is: except for the mahram males as stated in (Ayat 55) no other man should enter the Prophet’s (PBUH) houses and whoever has to ask some thing from the wives, should ask from behind a veil/curtain (hijab). After this command curtains were hung on the doors of the apartments of the wives, and since the Prophet’s (PBUH) house was/is a role model for all Muslim households to follow, they too hung curtains on their doors.
Note: This is the first time in the Quran that the word Hijab has been used.

All the above reforms deal with the issue of privacy in Islam: (i) Seek Permission before going to someone's home. (ii) Do not go to any occasion as uninvited guests (iii) Go on time – not too early or too late. (iv) Once you have eaten then leave (v) When speaking to the wives of the Prophet (PBUH) speak from behind a veil.

translation.text: It will not be blameworthy for the wives of the Prophet if their fathers, their sons, their brothers, their brothers' sons, their sisters' sons, and the women with whom they have social relations, and the persons whom their right hands possess enter their houses. (O women), shun disobeying Allah. Allah is watchful over everything.

commentary.text: Relatives before Whom a Woman does not need to observe Hijab include, father, sons, brothers, brother's sons or sister's sons, women friends, and slaves.

sections.title: 56-58 ALLAH HIMSELF AND HIS ANGELS SEND BLESSINGS ON THE PROPHET, O BELIEVERS INVOKE ALLAH'S BLESSINGS FOR HIM

translation.text: Indeed, Allah showers His blessings upon the Prophet, and His angels pray for him. O believers! Invoke Allah’s blessings upon him, and salute him with worthy greetings of peace.

commentary.text: Allah SWT is informing us about the Prophet (PBUH)’s high rank/status.
The Command to send blessing upon the Prophet
اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ عَبْدِكَ وَرَسُولِكَ، كَمَا صَلَّيْتَ عَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ ،
وَبَارِكْ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ، كَمَا بَارَكْتَ عَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيم
It is recommended to conclude supplications with blessing upon the Prophet
At-Tirmidhi recorded that Umar bin Al-Khattab said: "A supplication remains suspended between heaven and earth and does not ascend any further until you send Salah upon your Prophet.''

It is mandatory to send blessing upon the Prophet (PBUH) upon hearing the Prophet (PBUH) being mentioned. Thus one must say, " Sallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa- ala ālihi wa’ sallam” (Arabic: صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم) and in English (Peace be upon Him).

translation.text: Verily those who cause annoyance to Allah and His Messenger Allah has cursed them in this world and in the Hereafter and has prepared for them a humiliating chastisement.

commentary.text: (Also see 33: 61 and 64)
ALLAH SWT CURSES SUCH PEOPLE – so Beware!

Allah SWT warns and threatens those who annoy Him by going against His commands and doing that which He has forbidden, and who persist in doing so, and those who annoy His Messenger by accusing him of having faults or shortcomings.

Ironically and ultimately, they are only hurting and destroying themselves by committing these acts. Similarly, is we hurt or abuse someone else we hurt ourselves as wrong actions have consequences in this world and the next.

arabic_lines: وَالَّذِيۡنَ يُؤۡذُوۡنَ الۡمُؤۡمِنِيۡنَ وَالۡمُؤۡمِنٰتِ بِغَيۡرِ مَا اكۡتَسَبُوۡا فَقَدِ احۡتَمَلُوۡا بُهۡتَانًا وَّاِثۡمًا مُّبِيۡنًا

translation.text: As for those who abuse believing men and women unjustifiably, they will definitely bear the guilt of slander and blatant sin.

commentary.text: Now Allah SWT talks about his believing servants. Those who hurt believing men or women and they don’t deserve the hurt then such people have committed a grave sin and slander ا بُهۡتَانًا.

Slander ا بُهۡتَانًا means: ‘to ascribe a fault to a person that he/she does not have, or an error that he/she has not committed.’ The Prophet (PBUH) when asked about the meaning of backbiting said: “It is to make mention of your brother in a manner derogatory to him.” Then the questioner asked, “And if the fault is there in my brother?” The Prophet (PBUH) replied: “If the fault that you mentioned is there in him, you backbite him; if it is not there, you slandered him.”

Such an act is not only a moral sin, which will entail punishment in the Hereafter, but this Ayat also requires that in the law of an Islamic State false allegation should be held as a culpable offense. In Surah Nur the punishment for slander has been prescribed to be 80 lashes.
Hadith: A (true) Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hands all Muslims remain unharmed and safe.

sections.title: 59-59 COMMANDMENT OF HIJAB (DRESS CODE) FOR WOMEN

arabic_lines: يٰۤـاَيُّهَا النَّبِىُّ قُلْ لِّاَزۡوَاجِكَ وَبَنٰتِكَ وَنِسَآءِ الۡمُؤۡمِنِيۡنَ يُدۡنِيۡنَ عَلَيۡهِنَّ مِنۡ جَلَابِيۡبِهِنَّ ؕ ذٰ لِكَ اَدۡنٰٓى اَنۡ يُّعۡرَفۡنَ فَلَا يُؤۡذَيۡنَ ؕ وَكَانَ اللّٰهُ غَفُوۡرًا رَّحِيۡمًا

translation.text: O Prophet! Ask your wives, daughters, and believing women to draw their cloaks over their bodies. In this way it is more likely that they will be recognized ˹as virtuous˺ and not be harassed. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

commentary.text: Context: When believing women would go to the bathroom at night, they would get harassed/molested by the hypocrites thus Allah SWT sent this Ayat.
First the command of hijab was exclusively for the wives of the Prophet (PBUH). Now all believing women are being addressed.

Allah’s command/law requires that when a woman leaves the home then she should cover herself with a Jilbab جَلَابِيۡبِهِنَّ or a long loose outer garment. The word adna (from dunya) means to draw close or lower thus the jilbab should be wrapped around so as to cover the entire body. The object here was not to restrict the liberty of women but to protect them from harm and molestation. FYI – Head and chest covering has already been mentioned in surah Nur (Khimar).

These Ayat coupled with surah Nur Ayat 31, it becomes obvious that the intention of the command for a woman is to cover herself well to conceal her beautifications from others. (See below pg. 23 for a detailed explication.)

Thus, you should not come out of your houses in full makeup so as to display your beauty and physical charms before the greedy eyes of the people, rather it is best for women to come out in a simple, loose sheet fully concealing their adornments, and walking in a manner that does not attract attention.
Allah SWT will forgive the errors and mistakes that were committed due to ignorance, provided that you reform yourselves now when you have received clear guidance.

sections.title: 60-62 PUNISHMENT FOR THE HYPOCRITES AND SCANDAL MONGERS

translation.text: If the hypocrites, the sick at heart, and those who spread lies in the city do not desist, We shall rouse you [Prophet] against them, and then they will only be your neighbours in this city for a short while.
They shall be cursed from all around and they shall be ruthlessly killed wherever they are seized.

commentary.text: (Also see 33: 57 and 64)
ALLAH SWT CURSES SUCH PEOPLE – so Beware!
A Stern Warning to the Hypocrites and Slanders. Such people are cursed and they will find no peace nor blessing anywhere in the world. Allah SWT will deal with them very harshly.

Context: In order to cause chaos among the Muslims and to lower their morale, some people would spread rumors in Madinah to the effect that the Muslims had suffered such and such serious setback, that a huge army was gathering together against them, that Madinah was under threat of a sudden attack, etc. During the Battle of Ahzab some hypocrites who were weak of faith spread misinformation (fake news) resulting in fear and confusion.

Besides this, the hypocrisies had another pastime. They would concoct and spread imaginary stories about the domestic life of the Prophet’s (PBUH) household, for example, the incident of Aisha, so as to create suspicions among the common people and destroy the moral influence of the Muslims.

The reason why this punishment to seize and kill them has been awarded (although never executed) in such an absolute sense is because this matter relates to hypocrites who used to call themselves Muslims. But when a Muslim starts demonstrating open hostility to and denial of Islam, such a person is called: Murtadd: (Apostate/Renouncer) in the terminology of the Shari` ah. With such a man, there is no compromise in the Shari’ ah of Islam – except that he repents and reverts to Islam and accepts the injunctions of Islam in word and deed.

Allah SWT commands the believers to speak the truth and don’t water down facts meaning don’t speak in riddles or with ambiguity rather be clear and precise in speech no matter how difficulty the subject. This is a great burden and responsibility because when you speak the truth often it is not palatable to all. Mostly it is easier to go with the flow not causing any ripples.

Iman in Allah SWT and His Prophet (PBUH) = Great triumph
When we speak the truth Allah SWT’s blessings are with us. He will fill the deficiencies and forgive our sins.
He who obeys Allah SWT and His messenger has attained great success or triumph.

translation.text: We offered the trust  الۡاَمَانَةَ (amanat) to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to carry it and were afraid of doing so; but man carried it. Surely he is wrong-doing, ignorant.

commentary.text: Purpose of Life: Allah SWT wants man to realize his real position in the world and act/work accordingly. If, however, he regards this life of the world as mere fun and sport adopting a careless attitude then he is only working towards his own doom.

Here, the word “amanat” (trust) implies man's khilafat (caliphate) i.e. his Ruh (that Allah SWT blew into). According to the Quran, man has been granted khilafat on earth i.e. the freedom to choose between obedience and disobedience, as well as granted powers and authority over countless creations. Thus, man is then held responsible for his voluntary acts and deserves rewards for his righteous conduct and suffer punishment for his evil conduct.

In order to give us an idea of how important this “trust” (amanat) is, Allah SWT says that the heavens, the earth and the mountains, but in spite of their size and majesty, did not have the power and courage to accept. However, the weak and frail man accepted. With freedom of choice comes a great responsibly but most do not understand this huge burden.

Lesson: Every day we are make decisions/choices so be cognizant and choose wisely as this is a great blessing and responsibility has been bestowed upon us. We can either us it wisely or squander our chances for success.

Note: The presentation of the trust before the earth, heavens and the mountains and their fear/refusal to bear this ammant is this actually literal or figurative this only Allah SWT knows as we can neither know nor comprehend Allah SWT's relationship with His creations.

translation.text: (The consequence of man's carrying the trust is) that Allah may chastise hypocritical men and hypocritical women and accept the repentance of believing men and believing women. He is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.

commentary.text: The consequence of this "amanat" (trust) and the khilafat (caliphate) granted to mankind is for us to choose. Do we decide to take this "trust" lightly thus pursue our desires, doing exactly as we please, like the hypocrites/unbelievers. Or do we do what we were created for, that is, to worship and glorify our Raab. The choice is ours and the end is near!
Note: The surah began with don’t follow the disbelievers (33:1) and now ends with the punishment for the disbelievers.

items.text: COMMAND ONLY FOR THE WIVES OF PROPHET (PBUH)
Surah 33 Al-Ahzab (33:32, 33:33 and 33:53)

(33:32) Wives of the Prophet, you are not like other women. If you fear Allah, do not be too complaisant in your speech lest those with diseased hearts should covet you; but speak in a straightforward manner.

Speech: There is no harm if a man is spoken to in case of a genuine need, but on such an occasion the woman’s tone and manner of speech should be such as does not let the other man think that he could cherish any false hope from her. There should be no undue softness in her tone, no allurement in her conversation, no consciously affected mellowness in her voice, which should excite the male hearer’s emotions and encourage him to make advances.

(33:33) And stay in your homes and do not go about displaying your allurements as in the former Time of Ignorance. Establish Prayer, give Zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger. Allah only wishes to remove uncleanness from you, O members of the (Prophet's) household, and to purify you completely.

It is most preferable to remain at home and make your home the center of all activities including most importantly worship. However, if they have to move out of the house for an outdoor duty, they should not move out as the women used to do in the pre-Islamic days of ignorance. It does not behoove a Muslim woman to walk out fully made up in tightfitting or transparent dresses. These are the ways of ignorance that Islam does not approve.

(33:53) Believers, enter not the houses of the Prophet without his permission, nor wait for a meal to be prepared; instead enter when you are invited to eat, and when you have had the meal, disperse. Do not linger in idle talk. That is hurtful to the Prophet but he does not express it out of shyness; but Allah is not ashamed of speaking out the Truth. And if you were to ask the wives of the Prophet for something, ask from behind a curtain. (حِجَابٍ) (hijab) That is more apt for the cleanness of your hearts and theirs. It is not lawful for you to cause hurt to Allah's Messenger, nor to ever marry his wives after him. Surely that would be an enormous sin in Allah's sight. (First time the word Hijab is mentioned in the Quran).

In (Ahzab: 53) – "Hijab," means a physical curtain/veil between oneself and the speaker. Only the wives of the Prophet (PBUH) had to enforce this. However one should try and adopt all traits of the wives of the Prophet (PBUH) as they are the role models for all Believing women.
The word ḥijāb occurs 7 times the Qur’an (at 7:46, 17:45, 19:17, 33:53, 38:32, 41:5, 42:51).
A barrier between believers and deniers in the hereafter (7:46)
A barrier placed between the messenger and those who do not believe in the hereafter when he recites the Recitation or qur’ān (17:45)
A barrier or partition which Mary mother of Jesus placed between herself and her people (19:17)
A barrier or partition in the house of the prophet so that protocol might be observed between common believers and wives of the prophet (33:53)
A barrier or partition behind which the sun disappears at the end of the day (38:32)
A barrier or partition which prevents those who hear the message from understanding it (41:5)
A barrier from behind which God gives instruction to a mortal (42:51)
We can see that in none of these instances the Qur’an uses the term ḥijāb to mean clothing of any sort – female or otherwise

"Jilbab" means an extra covering/cloak so as to conceal any physical shape. (When leaving your home.)

Let them not stomp their feet, drawing attention to their hidden adornments. Turn to Allah in repentance all together, O believers, so that you may be successful.

"Khimar." means headscarf -- let them wear their khimar (headscarf) over their chest.  The woman of jahilya would wear a headscarf but not cover their chest. front_matter.text: The Surah takes its name from Ayat 15 in which the word Sheba has occurred (i. e. the Shebaeans).
